concept_name: Law of Conservation of Mass — Atoms Rearranged, Never Destroyed
section: Class 11 Chemistry Ch.1 'Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry', §1.3 Laws of Chemical Combination — Law of Conservation of Mass
source_book: NCERT Chemistry Class 11, Ch.1 'Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry', §1.3 — chapter-index scope reference only; teaching, examples, and phrasing authored from first principles. NCERT Exemplar consulted for misconception beliefs only (M1-M3), no problem text imported. Second chemistry concept through the pipeline.

real_world_anchor.primary: Charcoal on a barbecue grate or campfire burns down to a handful of ash that weighs almost nothing — anyone who has grilled or sat by a fire has watched kilograms seem to vanish into the air. That lived 'mass disappears' feeling is exactly the belief this concept breaks.
real_world_anchor.secondary: A sealed zip-top bag with baking soda and vinegar fizzes and swells, yet a kitchen scale reads the identical number before and after — a home-replicable proof that a closed system's mass never changes.

m_C.name: mass of carbon sample
m_C.role: integer_snap_required — rounding-robustness lock (chemistry block §3): a fractional step breaks the m_C + m_O2 = m_CO2 rounding identity

M_Fe.name: atomic mass of iron (teaching-rounded, IUPAC 55.85) — STATE_5 only

m_Fe_before_S5.name: STATE_5 staged constant — iron before rusting

m_gas_before_S5.name: STATE_5 staged constant — sealed O2 reservoir before

m_O2_reacted_S5.name: STATE_5 staged constant — oxygen mass that joins the solid

m_Fe_reacted_S5.name: STATE_5 staged constant — iron mass consumed (= 0.6 × 7/3)

m_O2.formula: m_C × 32/12 g — mass of oxygen consumed

m_CO2.formula: m_C × 44/12 g — mass of carbon dioxide formed

m_reactants.formula: m_C + m_O2 g — total reactant mass

reading_initial.formula: tare + m_C + (sealed ? m_O2 : 0) g — balance reading before reaction

reading_final.formula: tare + (sealed ? m_C + m_O2 : 0) g — balance reading after reaction

delta_reading.formula: reading_final − reading_initial g — net change (0 sealed, −m_CO2 open)

m_solid_after_S5.formula: m_Fe_before_S5 + m_O2_reacted_S5 g — STATE_5 solid readout after rusting

m_gas_after_S5.formula: m_gas_before_S5 − m_O2_reacted_S5 g — STATE_5 gas-reservoir readout after rusting

m_total_S5.formula: m_Fe_before_S5 + m_gas_before_S5 g — STATE_5 TOTAL, constant

constraints: atoms of each element: LHS count = RHS count in every displayed equation (C 1→1, O 2→2 for the symbol form)
total charge: LHS = RHS (= 0) in every displayed equation — no ions anywhere in this concept
no atom ever fades in or out on screen — atoms only MOVE between tiles (archetype-O signature); a departing gas atom must be shown leaving the frame, never disappearing in place
m_reactants ≡ m_CO2 identically, for every value of m_C — the STATE_4 balance needle centers at 0° deviation regardless of slider position
open-system reading_final = tare exactly (all reacted mass has left as escaped gas); sealed reading_initial = sealed reading_final = tare + m_C + m_O2 at every instant, not just at the two endpoints
no stoichiometric coefficient ever appears on screen — STATE_3/4/7's C(s)+O₂(g)→CO₂(g) is coefficient-free by construction (1:1:1); STATE_5's word equation never becomes a symbol equation
no oxidation-number label or redox electron-transfer ledger appears anywhere — both displayed reactions are technically redox but that analysis is out of scope, deferred to the redox chapter
m_C slider step is fixed at 1 (integer grams) — the displayed 1-dp closure of m_C + m_O2 = m_CO2 depends on this; a fractional step will produce a visible rounding mismatch

scene_composition.text: like charcoal burning down to ash on a grill

tts_sentences.text_en: Charcoal burns in an open pan sitting on a balance — like grilling over a campfire.
Watch the reading: fifty point zero grams, forty-nine point two, now forty-eight point one grams.
Almost two grams simply vanished from the scale — where did that mass go?

STATE_2.title: Seal It — The Reading Holds Level

scene_composition.text:
Mass never leaves the universe,
never arrives from nowhere — seal
the system and nothing is lost or gained.
sealed snack bag: soda + vinegar fizzes, scale doesn't move

tts_sentences.text_en: Same burn, twice: one pan open to the air, one sealed like a fizzing soda-and-vinegar bag.
The open pan's reading keeps falling, just like before.
The sealed side never moves, not even a tenth of a gram.
Mass never leaves the universe, never arrives from nowhere: seal the system and nothing is lost or gained.

misconception_watch.belief: Burning destroys matter — the mass just disappears.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The identical burn replayed sealed: the reading holds dead level while the open twin drops — the escaping wisps ARE the missing grams.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Mass never leaves the universe and never arrives from nowhere — seal the system and nothing is lost, nothing is gained.

STATE_3.title: Inside the Flask — Atoms Swap Partners

scene_composition.text:
Every substance is built from atoms — tiny
particles, each with its own fixed mass.

tts_sentences.text_en: Every substance is built from atoms — tiny particles, each with its own fixed mass.
Inside the sealed flask, one carbon atom C sits beside two oxygen atoms.
Watch carbon travel over and dock right between them — three atoms, same as before, just new partners.
Same atoms, new partners — that's carbon dioxide.

misconception_watch.belief: New substances mean new atoms — CO₂'s atoms are freshly made.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The CO₂ tile is built from the very same three atoms the reactants held.

tts_sentences.text_en: Twelve grams of carbon plus thirty-two grams of oxygen makes forty-four grams of carbon dioxide.
The ledger balances exactly — reactant mass equals product mass.
Drag the carbon slider — any amount you pick, the two sides still match.

STATE_5.title: Rusting — The Solid Gains, the Gas Loses

scene_composition.text:
2 atoms shown — representative; a
real nail involves billions
Same flask, now an iron nail + sealed oxygen

tts_sentences.text_en: An iron nail sits sealed inside a jar of oxygen, rusting instead of burning.
Oxygen atoms leave the gas and dock onto the iron's surface, one by one.
The solid gets heavier while the gas gets lighter, by the exact same amount.
The total never moves — the gain is oxygen's own mass changing address.

misconception_watch.belief: Rusting (or burning a metal) creates mass out of nowhere.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: Oxygen atoms visibly dock onto the iron while the gas-side reading falls by exactly as much as the solid rises; the TOTAL never moves.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: The gain is oxygen's own mass changing address.

STATE_6.title: Why It Holds — Mass Rides on Atoms

scene_composition.text: chemical reactions only — nuclear reactions are a different story

tts_sentences.text_en: Mass is just the sum: each atom's count times its atomic mass.
Before: one carbon at twelve, two oxygens at sixteen each, forty-four grams total.
The same count of atoms gives the same forty-four grams afterward.
The counts never change, so the mass never changes, true for chemical reactions, not nuclear ones.

STATE_7.title: Explore — Any Amount, Sealed or Open

scene_composition.equation_expr: {m_C.toFixed(1)} g C  +  {m_O2.toFixed(1)} g O₂  →  {m_CO2.toFixed(1)} g CO₂

tts_sentences.text_en: Drag carbon's mass and toggle sealed or open — watch every number update live, and the law hold.

regeneration_variants.label: Same law, a brighter burn (magnesium ribbon instead of charcoal)
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A magnesium ribbon burns in air with a bright white flame instead of charcoal; the same open-vs-sealed contrast and mass-ledger logic apply, just with magnesium's own ratios — the anchor reaction changes, not the law.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Identical conservation-of-mass reasoning: a sealed system holds steady, an open system loses the escaped or absorbed gas's mass; atoms rearrange, never vanish.

aha_moment.statement: Seal the flask and the balance doesn't move — matter is only rearranged, never destroyed.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: sealed reading holds flat at 82.0 g while the open reading drops to 48.1 g

assessment.mastery_definition: A student who reaches 80–85% understands: in a closed system, total mass is exactly conserved because a chemical reaction only rearranges atoms — it never creates or destroys them; an apparent mass loss (burning in open air) means a gaseous product escaped unweighed, and an apparent mass gain (rusting) means a gas's own mass transferred onto a solid; the same fixed 12:32:44-style ratio scales proportionally for any reactant amount; and the law holds because each atom's count and mass never change, valid for chemical (not nuclear) reactions.

questions.stem: A charcoal lump burns completely in an OPEN pan sitting on a kitchen scale. The reading falls from 50.0 g to 38.0 g. What happened to the missing 12.0 g?

options.A: It was destroyed by the fire — burning converts some mass into pure energy.
options.B: It escaped as invisible gas (carbon dioxide) that the open pan never weighed.
options.C: It evaporated into heat and light, which have no mass.
options.D: The scale simply drifted; no mass actually left the system.

distractor_misconceptions.A: the burning-destroys-mass misconception (M1) — believes matter converts to energy in an ordinary chemical reaction
distractor_misconceptions.C: confuses heat/light (energy) with mass loss — no mass is carried away as heat
distractor_misconceptions.D: denies the observation instead of explaining it — evades the physics

questions.tested_idea: an escaping gaseous product carries mass away in an open system

questions.stem: The same burn is repeated inside a SEALED flask. What happens to the balance reading?

options.A: It falls by the same 12.0 g as the open pan, since burning still destroys mass.
options.B: It holds perfectly steady — nothing can leave a closed system, so total mass cannot change.
options.C: It falls, but by less than the open pan, since some gas is trapped.
options.D: It rises, since the trapped gas adds weight to the flask.

distractor_misconceptions.A: the burning-destroys-mass misconception (M1), untouched by the sealed-system evidence
distractor_misconceptions.C: invents partial escape from a system that is, by definition, sealed
distractor_misconceptions.D: confuses 'trapped gas exists' with 'trapped gas adds NEW mass' — the gas's mass was already counted in the reactants

questions.tested_idea: closed system ⇒ total mass is exactly conserved, not just approximately
questions.parallel_form_stem: A student burns identical wood samples in an open fireplace and inside a sealed glass jar. Which reading changes, and why?

questions.stem: In C(s) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g), where do the atoms in the CO₂ molecule come from?

options.A: They are newly created when the bond forms.
options.B: They are the exact same carbon and oxygen atoms that were in the reactants, just rearranged.
options.C: Only the oxygen atoms are new; carbon is destroyed.
options.D: Half the atoms are created and half survive from the reactants.

distractor_misconceptions.C: invents an atom being destroyed mid-reaction
distractor_misconceptions.D: invents a partial-creation compromise with no basis in the reaction

questions.tested_idea: atoms are rearranged, never created or destroyed, in a chemical reaction

questions.stem: 18.0 g of carbon burns completely in oxygen. Using the fixed ratio 12 g C : 32 g O₂ : 44 g CO₂, how much CO₂ forms, and how much O₂ was used?

options.A: 48.0 g O₂ used; 66.0 g CO₂ formed.
options.B: 32.0 g O₂ used; 44.0 g CO₂ formed (same as the 12 g case).
options.C: 18.0 g O₂ used; 30.0 g CO₂ formed.
options.D: There isn't enough information — the ratio only works for exactly 12 g of carbon.

distractor_misconceptions.B: assumes the 12:32:44 ratio is a fixed absolute, not a scalable ratio — reuses the default numbers regardless of the actual carbon mass
distractor_misconceptions.C: a proportional-reasoning slip — scales carbon linearly but miscalculates the O₂ and CO₂ amounts
distractor_misconceptions.D: believes the conservation ratio is a special case rather than a general proportional law

questions.tested_idea: the 12:32:44 mass ratio scales proportionally for any amount of carbon
questions.parallel_form_stem: 6.0 g of carbon burns completely. How much oxygen is used and how much CO₂ forms?

questions.stem: An iron nail rusts inside a sealed jar of oxygen. The solid iron/rust reading rises by 0.6 g. What happened to the sealed gas reading?

options.A: It also rose by 0.6 g, since oxygen was added to the system.
options.B: It fell by exactly 0.6 g — the same oxygen atoms that joined the solid left the gas.
options.C: It stayed the same, since rusting doesn't consume any gas.
options.D: It fell by more than 0.6 g, since rusting also releases some gas.

distractor_misconceptions.A: the mass-creation misconception (M2) — believes rusting manufactures new mass instead of transferring it
distractor_misconceptions.C: denies that rusting consumes oxygen gas at all
distractor_misconceptions.D: invents an extra gas-release process with no basis in this reaction

questions.tested_idea: a solid's mass gain during rusting is exactly balanced by the gas's mass loss — transfer, not creation

questions.stem: WHY does total mass stay exactly the same before and after any chemical reaction?

options.A: Because energy released by the reaction exactly cancels any mass change.
options.B: Because the number of atoms of each element, and each atom's mass, never changes — only their partners change.
options.C: Because chemical reactions are always too slow to lose measurable mass.
options.D: Because most reactions happen in sealed containers by default.

distractor_misconceptions.A: invents an energy-mass cancellation with no basis for ordinary chemical reactions — that is a nuclear-scale effect, outside this law's scope
distractor_misconceptions.C: confuses reaction RATE with mass conservation — irrelevant to the physics
distractor_misconceptions.D: reverses cause and effect — sealing is what lets us OBSERVE conservation, not the reason it holds

questions.tested_idea: mass conservation follows from fixed atom counts and fixed atomic masses, valid for chemical (non-nuclear) reactions
questions.parallel_form_stem: A teacher says mass conservation would fail inside a nuclear reactor. Is this consistent with what this law claims?
